title: Field Pilot Canvas & Orientation Brief
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working kickoff canvas for the Field Pilot with Meridian Logistics (internal codename: FieldPilot). It captures the scope, minimal viable success criteria, acceptance tests, workshop orientation, quick deployment notes, and immediate action items. This is intentionally pragmatic — lean checklist for the first 30 days.

Context and goals:
- Customer: Meridian Logistics — supply-chain planning and customer support use cases (chat summarization, route-exception classification).
- Engagement type: 30-day field pilot (small production footprint) using Redwood Dedicated capacity with optional Private sync for sensitive manifests.
- Primary objective: demonstrate predictable latency (<150ms p95 for short-turn chat flows) and 5x cost improvement vs current baseline for batch reranking.

Scope (what we will deliver in 30 days):
- Integration of Redwood API for chat + rerank endpoints into Meridian’s support app for a single route.
- Two evaluation datasets: live support transcripts (anonymized) and historical routing exceptions (10k rows).
- Dashboard access in Redwood Console for three routes: chat-gen, rerank, embeddings lookup.
- Canary deployment plan and rollback policy for cutover to pilot model.

Out-of-scope (explicit):
- Full org-wide deployment, custom model training, long-term SLA contracts, HIPAA compliance package (unless contracted).

Success criteria (firm acceptance):
Quantitative:
- Latency: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 150ms for chat-generation calls at expected concurrency (30 concurrent users simulated).
- Cost: per-request token cost reduced by >= 4x vs Meridian’s current hosted endpoint for the rerank workflow when using batching/caching.
- Accuracy proxy: rerank top-1 match rate >= 82% on holdout set (Meridian-supplied eval set).
- Availability: 99.5% uptime observed over the 30-day window for the pilot routes.

Qualitative:
- CS team reports that responses are coherent and context-aware in at least 80% of sampled conversations (human review).
- Product manager signs off that the integration flow is operational and the rollback plan is tested.

Acceptance tests (how we verify):
- Synthetic load test: SRE to run a 2-hour simulated traffic run at 1.5x expected concurrency and capture p50/p95. (Ticket: JIRA-8821-loadtest)
- Eval run: Run rerank eval against 10k historical cases — record top-1 match rate and AUC.
- User review: 40 random chat exchanges flagged for human review; annotate pass/fail for coherence.
- Failover test: Trigger capacity fallback to alternate model variant and observe graceful degradation (no more than 2x latency increase).

Roles & responsibilities:
- Meridian: provide anonymized transcript dump, routing dataset, and product contact (Nora Chen).
- Redwood Solutions (owner: Priya Shah): lead integration, run canary, own success measurement and SLO reporting to Meridian.
- Platform Eng (Marco Diaz): provision Dedicated pool, assist with VPC peering if Private option is chosen.
- Applied ML (Leah Kim): pick model variants, quantization profile for cost targets, evaluate results.
- SRE (Jordan Park): run load tests, configure alerting in Console.

Workshop / Kickoff agenda (90 min on Day 0) — draft:
- 0–10 min: Introductions + engagement objectives (Priya)
- 10–25 min: Meridian product context + key risk areas (Meridian PM)
- 25–40 min: Technical architecture walkthrough (Marco)
- 40–60 min: Data & privacy checklist; anonymization requirements (legal / product)
- 60–80 min: Success criteria & acceptance tests (Leah)
- 80–90 min: Immediate next actions and owners (round-robin)

Data & access checklist (must before Day 3):
- Anonymized transcript CSV (schema spec attached in Confluence link).
- Historical routing matrix (CSV, 10k rows), sample of 200 rows for early eval.
- API keys for staging environment + list of service IPs for allowlisting.
- If Private option chosen: network diagram and KMS details.

Minimal deployment plan (steps for first 14 days):
1) Staging integration (days 0–3): wire up Redwood API keys in Meridian staging, smoke test with sample prompts.
2) Eval run (days 3–7): Applied ML runs rerank eval and produces report; iterate prompts.
3) Canary (days 8–12): Deploy to 5% of production traffic with dedicated pool; monitor latency, error rates.
4) Pilot scale (days 13–30): Expand to full pilot scope, daily report to Meridian.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Sensitive PII in transcripts. Mitigation: require strict anonymization; Redwood will refuse any PII payloads in staging logs and enable redaction hooks.
- Risk: Unexpected latency spikes under production traffic. Mitigation: Canary + autoscaling policies; fallback model variant.
- Risk: Dataset not representative. Mitigation: run small sampling eval and adjust acceptance thresholds or collect additional samples.

Open questions (to resolve in first 48h):
- Are there retention/legal requirements that prevent storing any logs longer than X days? (Meridian to confirm)
- Which route in the product is most business-critical for pilot? Meridian to choose between Support Flow A or Routing Flow B.
- Does Meridian want private KMS integration or is Dedicated with encrypted-at-rest sufficient?

Immediate action items (owners):
- Meridian: share anonymized sample and designate PM contact (due: 2025-11-14)
- Priya: create JIRA epic and add evaluation tickets; schedule Day 0 workshop (due: 2025-11-13)
- Marco: provision staging Dedicated pool; provide connection instructions (due: 2025-11-16)
- Leah: draft eval harness and metric definitions for rerank (due: 2025-11-18)
- Jordan: prepare load test script and baseline runbook (due: 2025-11-20)

Notes to self / internal reminders (informal):
- Keep acceptance bar conservative — we can always relax thresholds after qualitative signoff.
- Watch for class imbalance in routing dataset — sampling to be done before model choice.
- Prep two model variants: one quantized for cost, one fp16 for comparison.

References:
- CONFLUENCE-FieldPilot-Onboarding-542 (data spec)
- JIRA-8821 (pilot epic)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/solutions/pull/456 (integration scaffold)

Next update cadence: daily stand for first 7 days, then tri-weekly summary to Meridian PM.
